report_name: LiteLLM Supply Chain Attack Steals Cloud and AI Service Keys

attack_patterns.name: Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools
attack_patterns.description: Attackers compromised the LiteLLM project's release pipeline to publish a malicious version (v1.107.0) to PyPI and Docker Hub, representing a classic software supply chain attack.

attack_patterns.name: Unsecured Credentials
attack_patterns.description: The malicious LiteLLM package was designed to scan the compromised environment for sensitive credentials stored in environment variables (e.g., AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, OPENAI_API_KEY) and configuration files (e.g., ~/.aws/credentials).

attack_patterns.name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
attack_patterns.description: After harvesting credentials from the environment, the malware exfiltrated them to an attacker-controlled server.

malware.name: LiteLLM Credential Harvester
malware.description: A trojanized component embedded within LiteLLM version 1.107.0, designed to harvest sensitive credentials such as cloud provider logins, developer secrets, and AI service API keys from the environment and exfiltrate them to an attacker-controlled server.

tools.name: LiteLLM
tools.description: The legitimate open-source AI gateway tool whose release pipeline was compromised. Version 1.107.0 was trojanized to deliver a credential harvesting payload.

identities.name: LiteLLM Users
identities.description: Downstream users and organizations who installed the malicious LiteLLM v1.107.0 from PyPI or Docker Hub, becoming victims of credential theft.

identities.name: PyPI
identities.description: The Python Package Index (PyPI) was abused as a distribution channel for the malicious LiteLLM package v1.107.0.

identities.name: Docker Hub
identities.description: The Docker Hub registry was abused as a distribution channel for malicious LiteLLM container images tagged v1.107.0, latest, main-latest, and main-stable.

identities.name: OpenAI
identities.description: AI service provider whose API keys were a primary target for theft by the malicious LiteLLM package.

identities.name: Anthropic
identities.description: AI service provider whose API keys were a primary target for theft by the malicious LiteLLM package.

infrastructure.name: Attacker Exfiltration Server
infrastructure.description: An attacker-controlled server used to receive credentials exfiltrated by the malicious LiteLLM package.

indicators.name: Malicious LiteLLM PyPI Dependency Installation
indicators.pattern:
title: Malicious LiteLLM PyPI Dependency Installation
id: 2b1c8e9f-a0b1-4c2d-8e3f-4a5b6c7d8e9f
status: experimental
description: Detects the installation of the compromised LiteLLM version 1.107.0 via pip command line.
references:
  - https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/10/22/litellm-compromised-supply-chain-attack-pypi-docker/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-22
tags:
  - attack.t1195.001
level: critical
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/pip'
      - '/pip3'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'install'
      - 'litellm==1.107.0'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the installation of the compromised LiteLLM version 1.107.0 via pip, as identified in the hunting hints.

indicators.name: Malicious LiteLLM Docker Image Pull
indicators.pattern:
title: Malicious LiteLLM Docker Image Pull
id: 9f8e7d6c-5b4a-4c3d-8e2f-1a0b9c8d7e6f
status: experimental
description: Detects a pull of the compromised LiteLLM Docker image. Note that 'latest' tags are only malicious if pulled during the incident window (Oct 21, 2026, 11:46-14:20 UTC).
references:
  - https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/10/22/litellm-compromised-supply-chain-attack-pypi-docker/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-22
tags:
  - attack.t1195.001
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_base:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/docker'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'pull'
      - 'litellm'
  selection_tags:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - ':v1.107.0'
      - ':latest'
      - ':main-latest'
      - ':main-stable'
  condition: selection_base and 1 of selection_tags
indicators.description: Detects the pull of a compromised LiteLLM Docker image via command line, as identified in the hunting hints. The malicious tags were v1.107.0, latest, main-latest, and main-stable during the incident window.
